title: Endoscope objective optical system, US11543647B2 example 1

aperture_validity.basis: the aperture stop is a plate in the air space between the second and third groups, with an opening smaller than the surfaces beside it
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: eligibility only: a stop-dependent match needs evidence (a field point or pupil sample), which this batch does not assert

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 546.07 nm. The publication's index column is headed ne and its description states that ne is the e-line index (vd is the Abbe number at the d line), so the record is evaluated at the e line. Converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact)
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states indices at the d line only. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; the single d-line index pair does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial effective focal length of the native Project.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial distance from the last optical surface vertex to the rear focal point for collimated input.

total_track_mm.definition: Axial distance from the first optical surface to the image plane.

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length. atol = 0.005 mm is half a unit in the last decimal of the coarsest focal length these publications print (two decimals); rtol = 2e-3 is 1e-3 for a prescription printed to four decimals on radii as small as 0.27 mm plus 1e-3 for the engine's air-referenced index convention

effective_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

back_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

comparison.why: the publication states neither an effective focal length nor a back focal length for this example, so the two-quantity rule has no pair to judge. The engine's values are recorded under engine_check as ENGINE_COMPUTED facts and no verdict is claimed

nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.note: the publication states an F-number, a half angle of view and an image height, but no effective focal length, so no source-stated first-order value exists to compare against

nominal_back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the paraxial image point

f_number.definition: image-space f-number as the publication states it

field.definition: the publication states a half angle of view omega; it does not say whether the value is a half or a full field, and this record does not convert one into the other
field.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the publication's parameter table: omega 66.3 deg)
field.convention_note: recorded as the source states it. A half field of 66.3 deg with an image height of 0.5 mm and the engine's 0.5267 mm focal length would put the chief ray at 1.20 mm, not 0.5 mm, so either omega is a full field, or the image height is a half height, or the two are stated under different conditions. The mismatch is left open rather than resolved by assumption

materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd. A patent table gives nd and vd only, which cannot define a dispersion curve; fitting one would invent a material. Published catalog glasses were compared as a cross-check and are recorded under catalog_comparisons, never substituted.

approximations.detail: every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd; the source's vd is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the e line (546.07 nm air), the line the source's ne column states; every glass is a constant index, so the choice of line moves no first-order value

the source states no clear apertures; semi-diameters were derived from the stated F-number and field and set to 0.45-0.58 mm clear radius (0.90-1.16 mm element diameter, in the range an endoscope tip allows), edged 0.02 mm beyond the clear aperture. They set the stop plate and the solid checks, not the first-order values

surface 6 of the source table is a plane with air on both sides and a zero spacing to the stop; it was merged away and its zero spacing added to the stop's spacing, so no zero-thickness row reaches the format
the source states no object distance; the Project is built for an object at infinity, which is the source's own 'focused from a near point up to a far point' reading with the near point not stated
the source gives no stop-plate outer radius; the plate reaches the largest clear semi-diameter beside the stop
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled

with derived clear apertures, seven glass members sit above the engine's 35 % edge-thickness review ratio (46-111 % of their clear diameter). This is a property of a 1 mm-class endoscope objective with no stated apertures, not a geometry error: the engine reports it as INFO and the optical-solid check stays VALID

notes: evaluated at the e line (546.07 nm air, 546.219159071447 nm vacuum) because the source's index column is ne
project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0
project solids reported no error-severity finding

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the publication states no effective focal length or back focal length, so there is no source-stated first-order value to compare the engine's 0.526739 mm EFL and -0.006470 mm BFL against
the source's stated half field, image height and the engine's focal length are mutually inconsistent (see field.convention_note); this record does not resolve the mismatch
no field verification: this batch built no per-field configurations, so no field-dependent quantity is asserted

record_hash_method: SHA-256 over this record's JSON with the record_hash and record_hash_method members removed: json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) encoded as UTF-8, no trailing newline. Recompute it from the committed record.json after parsing the JSON, not from the file's bytes.
